title: Hosted API microburst spillover & prewarm plan — peak projections (Nov 2026)
sheet_text:
Objective:
Provide a compact operational plan that ties projected 15s/1m microburst profiles to concrete prewarm reservations and cross-region spillover policies for the Hosted API fleet. Focus is on tokens/sec and QPS headroom targets by GPU family and AZ for Nov-Dec 2026 peak window.

Executive summary:
- We expect three distinct microburst modalities in the Nov–Dec promo window: distributed microbursts (many small users), concentrated flashes (few customers driving heavy bursts), and correlated market-driven spikes (region-wide).
- Baseline 95th pct tokens/sec across global frontends projected: 2.1M t/s. 99.9th microburst peaks (15s buckets) projection: 6.6M t/s.
- Target operational headroom: reserve 35% of equivalent steady-state capacity as fast-prewarmable fabric + 10% cross-region spillable pool. This yields an effective tactical headroom of ~45% during peak windows.
- Recommended prewarm strategy: lightweight prewarm reservations on H100 pools (fast warmup lanes) + opportunistic prewarm on mixed A100/L40 capacity for non-latency-critical workloads.

Assumptions (short):
- Model mix: 60% chat-dense models (kv-cache heavy), 25% instruction-ish gen, 15% embedding/encode-only traffic.
- Average token length per request: 60 tokens.
- Tokenization variance accounted for with +12% safety margin.
- Prewarm ramp time to usable KV-cache state: H100: 6s median, A100-80GB: 18s median (measured from snapshot tests).
- Spillover network RTT constraint: prefer cross-region spill if extra latency <= +70ms tail for 95th pct.

Key tables (15s buckets):
Regional peak projections (15s window) — tokens/sec equivalent and QPS estimate
| Region | 95p t/s (steady) | 99.9p t/s (15s) | 15s QPS est (avg req tokens=60) | Observed burst type |
| us-west | 340,000 | 1,080,000 | 567 | distributed |
| us-east | 420,000 | 1,320,000 | 693 | concentrated |
| eu-west | 300,000 | 900,000 | 472 | correlated |
| ap-south | 160,000 | 480,000 | 252 | distributed |
| total | 1,220,000 | 3,780,000 | 1,984 | mixed |

GPU fabric headroom by family (fast-path vs warmable):
| GPU family | baseline tokens/sec equiv | fast-prewarm pool target (%) | reserved slots (vGPU units) | latency SLO impact |
| H100-80GB | 520,000 | 35% | 80 vunits | +/- 5ms tail if used |
| A100-80GB | 420,000 | 20% | 60 vunits | +/- 12ms tail |
| L40 | 280,000 | 10% | 40 vunits | +/- 20ms tail |
| mixed-burst-pool (cpu+gpu) | 0 | 10% (spill) | dynamic | fallthrough |

Prewarm reservation mechanics (operational knobs):
- Fast lanes (H100): keep warm snapshots sized for top-2 model variants; prewarm ratio = 0.35 * region_peak_capacity per AZ. Snapshots expire after 90s of inactivity.
- A100 lanes: opportunistic prewarm for long-tail customers; use predictive prewarm signals from traffic classifier.
- Spillover policy: when AZ utilization > 78% and microburst predicted to exceed 2x baseline in next 15s, trigger spill to nearest compatible region with spare spill pool until utilization < 62%.
- Metering: attribute prewarm consumption to route-level bucket for billing + SLO chargeback.

Cost and efficiency table (monthlyized estimate for 2-week promo window):
| Item | Extra reserved vunits (avg) | Estimated cost delta (USD) | Notes |
| prewarm-H100 | 80 vunits * 14 days avg | $46,800 | reserved on-demand vs spot delta included |
| opportunistic-A100 | 40 vunits * 14 days avg | $18,200 | heavily utilized by background workloads |
| cross-region-network | n/a | $4,200 | egress and inter-AZ overhead for spill events |
| total window delta | n/a | $69,200 | rough estimate, rounded |

Operational runbook (short bullets):
- T-72h: enable predictive prewarm mode and raise H100 target from 15% to 35% in flagged regions.
- T-12h: run smoke sweep of snapshot integrity and KV-cache restore latency tests per AZ. Abort prewarm if restore P99 > target (20s).
- T-0 to +4h (peak window): 1-minute cadence telemetry on tokens/sec, queued requests, KV-cache hit %, and region-utilization heatmap. Auto-trigger spill policy when thresholds hit.
- Post-peak +24h: revert H100 target to baseline (15%); capture anomalies and tag customer traffic patterns for model-specific adjustments.

Failure modes & mitigations:
- Slow snapshot restore on A100: fallback to model-variant routing to lower memory variant + route-level 503 gating for heavy tails.
- Spillfront congestion (unexpected RTT increase): throttle spill and instead reduce model-size for sampled requests.
- Sudden global correlated spike: engage emergency throttle policy and prioritize SLA customers; begin fast scale of dedicated pools if 503 rate > 0.2% and sustained > 5m.

Telemetry and alerts (practical thresholds):
- Headline alerts: region tokens/sec > 90% reserved capacity for 30s -> P1 runbook.
- Microburst alert: 15s token delta > 2.5x baseline -> trigger spill decision pipeline.
- Prewarm health: KV-restore P95 > 12s or P99 > 20s -> degrade prewarm ratio by 50% and page infra run.

Action items (owners):
- Maya: add predictive prewarm classifier flags to traffic router (INF-4221) — due 2026-11-06.
- Jamal: simulate cross-region spill latency matrices and update nearest-region mapping (load tests by 2026-11-08).
- Connor: run cost sensitivity for H100 reserved vs spot across all regions and produce final window budget (due 2026-11-09).
- Eleanor: coordinate T-12h smoke sweep and final sign-off with SRE on 2026-11-10.

Notes / open questions:
- Consider adding model-preserving quantized snapshots to reduce prewarm size for L40 lanes (low effort R&D spike required).
- Need tighter telemetry linking tokens->customer_id to perform per-customer throttles without violating privacy retention policies (legal sign-off required).

Appendix: quick synthetic sim outputs (selected):
- Single-customer concentrated flash (us-east): baseline 45k t/s -> 15s peak 620k t/s -> spill required to us-west within 6s to keep P99 latency < 400ms.
- Distributed microburst (eu-west): 15k concurrent small bursts -> graceful absorption by 25% opportunistic A100 pool.

End of sheet.
